findings.issue_text: The migration dereferences `[0]['id']` before applying its fallback, so a blank, deleted, or renamed `embed_category` can produce no rows and crash the migration.
The migration inserts existing host settings without URL/path normalization, so values such as `https://example.com/path` are stored verbatim and no longer match URI-host lookups.
Hosts with ports such as `example.com:3000` can be saved, but lookup strips the port via `URI(...).host`, so those records can never match requests.
There is no normalized-host uniqueness constraint, allowing duplicate hosts with different categories; `where(...).first` then selects an unspecified category.
Removing the allowed-host check makes existing embedded topics expandable whenever `embed_truncate` is enabled, even after all embedding hosts are removed.

goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hosts with ports such as `example.com:3000` can be saved, but lookup strips the port via `URI(...).host`, so those records can never match requests.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is correct. Looking at the diff, in `app/models/embeddable_host.rb`, the `record_for_host` method uses `URI(host).host` which strips the port from the URL. However, the validation regex `validates_format_of :host, :with => /\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\/i` explicitly allows ports (the `(:[0-9]{1,5})?` part). The `before_validation` callback only strips the protocol and path, not the port. So a host like `example.com:3000` can be saved to the database, but when `record_for_host` is called with a URL like `http://example.com:3000/page`, it extracts just `example.com` (without port) and queries `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`, which won't match `example.com:3000` stored in the database.

adjudication_records.issue_text: There is no normalized-host uniqueness constraint, allowing duplicate hosts with different categories; `where(...).first` then selects an unspecified category.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is valid. Looking at the diff, the EmbeddableHost model (app/models/embeddable_host.rb) has no uniqueness validation or database constraint on the 'host' column. The migration (db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb) creates the table with just 'host' and 'category_id' columns but no unique index. The `record_for_host` method uses `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` which would return an arbitrary record if duplicates exist. This means users could add the same host multiple times with different categories, and the system would non-deterministically pick one when determining which category to use for embedded topics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removing the allowed-host check makes existing embedded topics expandable whenever `embed_truncate` is enabled, even after all embedding hosts are removed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in app/models/topic.rb, the `expandable_first_post?` method was changed from checking `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? && SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` to just `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`. This removes the check for whether any embeddable hosts exist. The finding correctly identifies that this means existing embedded topics will show as expandable whenever `embed_truncate` is enabled, even if all embedding hosts have been removed from the new EmbeddableHost table. This is a behavioral change that could be unintended - the original code required embeddable_hosts to be configured, but the new code doesn't check if any EmbeddableHost records exist.
